milestone:
M7: advanced coaching, in 59 small PRs across 15 tracks. It covers:
- a whole-schedule load model by system, built on M1's acute:chronic EWMA and M6's daily loads, so Train, the coach and Progress agree
- one week evaluator, built on M3's interference rules and extended with load-, priority- and event-aware rules, judging Train, moves, the coach, the generator and M6's weekly review, plus a deterministic scheduler that repairs a week, for generated weeks and, through the coach, for the owner's own
- goal priorities from rank and event proximity, with goal modes and maintenance doses built on M3's own maintenance split
- block types as week plans: strength phases, hypertrophy, marathon and half, fight camp, maintenance, deloads, tapers and recovery
- VDOT paces (marathon pace on M3's steady segment kind) and heart-rate zones
- generator hooks that M6's cycle review inherits, and M6's week targets that judge M7 weeks by their own plan
- re-plans stored as program versions and proposed through M5's lifecycle, started by Profile goal changes, the weekly review's fatigue signals and the coach, with the weekly review deciding, refreshing and narrating a deload like its own proposals
- five coach tools, and a draft-free path for the scheduler's repair through propose_program_adjustment
- calm Train findings, the 'why' behind every placement, week-kind indicators and a season timeline
- the multi-discipline journey, and a rules reference generated from a registry of constants and behaviours

CONTEXT LOADING AND TRANSACTIONS (recorded in the periodisation-engine ADR).
- No M7 read races a JS timer. A query abandoned by a timer keeps its connection busy, the caller's next query queues behind it on that client (which one-query-per-client.ts fails), and a cancel would abort the caller's transaction.
- On the pool (Train's load, getMoveTargets, Today, the coach's turn facts), the reads run in one short read-only transaction with SET LOCAL statement_timeout: 300 ms per statement for the context, 250 ms for the coach's week block. A cancelled statement (SQLSTATE 57014) gives null, an app_errors row and checkWeek's fallback.
- Inside a caller's transaction (createWeeklyReview, M5's batch inside acceptProposal, the replan accept, proposeReplan inside a review), the reads run in a read-only savepoint with the same SET LOCAL.
  - The savepoint is always rolled back to after the reads, which are already in memory.
  - Postgres undoes the SET LOCAL at that rollback, and a timeout error ends with the savepoint.
  - So the transaction carries on, one query at a time on its own connection.
- A caller that opens its own transaction loads the context first, on the pool, and passes it in (M3's moveSession).
- The weekly review builds its context from its own facts loader (deps.facts), so the context adds no fact query to the review's transaction.
- Each such path has a stall test: a reader that runs pg_sleep on the executor it is given, under the one-query guard. The transaction commits on checkWeek's fallback with zero overlaps.

THE LOAD MODEL (ADR proposed in m7-contract, accepted in docs-m7). It extends M1's and M6's load code instead of duplicating it, so Train, the coach, Progress and the weekly review agree.
- Systems: lower body, upper body, aerobic, combat and CNS.
- A session's load is M1's sRPE (minutes × RPE) through M3's sessionLoadOf, exactly as M6's sessionLoads computes it, split by the data shares in rules/load.ts:
  - strength: by each region's hard sets, with CNS from heavy sets
  - runs: by type, with a lower-body impact share; intervals add CNS
  - Muay Thai: by format; sparring adds CNS and lower
  - mobility: 0
- Unknown values follow M6's rule. A logged session with no RPE or no duration is 'load unknown': counted and named, and left out of totals, never 0. A planned session uses its target RPE. DEFAULT_RPE fills only a missing target, and that load is kept as a separate, labelled 'estimated' series.
- Logged sessions come from M6's facts loader (completed, undeleted workouts only) and replace planned ones up to today:
  - a completed planned session counts once
  - a skipped one never counts
  - an unlogged past one counts 0 and is flagged missed
- Per system:
  - a residual with its half-life, which needs no history
  - the acute:chronic ratio, from M1's acuteChronicRatio over that system's daily series: null under 28 days of history, as Progress shows it
  - a level of fresh, elevated or overloaded. Before 28 days, days 14 to 27 included, the level comes from the residual alone, against a typical hard session taken from the plan.
- Total logged load per day equals M6's dailyLoads for the same facts, as tested.
- The generator projects from the plan alone; the services add the logs. Train renders no load numbers.

ONE EVALUATOR, RULES AS DATA, ONE REGISTRY.

- It returns findings {rule, severity, days, sessions, headline, message, why, resolution?, actionable}, a 0–100 score and a grade: clear, minor or conflicts.
- M3's four rules run unchanged through checkWeek, and M3's tests stay as they are. With no context, every surface falls back to checkWeek.
- M7's rules join when the context carries load, priorities, the week kind or events:

  - run_volume_vs_leg_strength
  - same_day_priority_order (it replaces same_day_order only when priorities are given) and same_day_separation
  - event_protection, recovery_week_limits and sparring_cap
- Costs are weighted by the harmed goal's weight, and a kept conflict carries a trade-off sentence naming both goals.
- The scheduler (repairWeek) can keep the owner's moves (the generator and M6's review always do) or not: an owner-facing suggestion may move the owner's own conflicting session. Its moves come out as M3 moveSession ops.
- rules/registry/ holds one RuleEntry per rule. Its id is the rule key decisions cite, and its status is active or superseded (with supersededBy). It is one of two kinds:
  - constant: source 'path#EXPORT', with values read from the live constant
  - behaviour: source 'path#function', the function that applies the rule, with no values (goals.paused, days.free_days, edits.move and the like)
- m7-contract creates one placeholder file per area, m3, m4 and m6 included. Exactly one slice fills each area, except generator.ts, which the serial generator chain appends to. Each area file may export a supersedes map, which index.ts applies, so no area file is edited twice.

GOAL PRIORITY.
- Shaping goals are M3's: input.maintenance ? input.paused : input.goals. With every open goal paused, each is at maintenance with no leader, and the season is one maintenance block over input.paused, as M3 plans it. Otherwise paused goals are left out, as in M3.
- Rank weights: 1, 0.6, 0.4, 0.25 and 0.15.
- Who leads: inside its lead window (fight 8, marathon 16, half 12, meet 10, other race 6 weeks), an event goal leads over every goal whose own event is outside its window. Two in-window events are resolved by rank. A passed event drops out.
- Modes:
  - primary: the leader
  - secondary: a goal with at least half the leader's weight that does not conflict with it. CONFLICTS pairs are data with reasons: fight camp or marathon build/peak against a hypertrophy emphasis, marathon peak/taper against strength gain, and meet prep against hypertrophy.
  - maintenance: every other goal
- Every verdict has a sentence naming the goals, the dates and the rule.
- prepare (stages/prepare.ts) reorders input.goals, disciplines and refs by effective priority at the block's start, and sets an optional input.modes, so M3's allocation, split choice and placement follow the leader. The stored input snapshot stays the original.
- Doses build on M3:
  - strength and hypertrophy at maintenance: M3's maintenance split, read live (Keep A and Keep B, 2 sets a slot, 4–10 hard sets per major group), with the main lifts' top set capped at RPE 8
  - a secondary strength or hypertrophy goal keeps its own layout and style (one chooseSplit hunk), held to the lower half of its own HARD_SET_RANGES band: 8–11 sets for strength, 10–15 for hypertrophy
  - runs: 60–70 % of recent volume, at most one quality session, the long run held
  - Muay Thai: technique and pads, with no sparring unless it is a class
- doseBand(split, phase, mode) is the one function that turns a mode into a set band. The generator, M6's targets.ts and the reviews all call it.
- allocateWeek (one hunk) caps dosed streams and gives the freed days to the leader.
- The maintenance block type puts every goal at its dose (maintenanceWeeks). It is used:
  - when every goal is paused (M3's case)
  - between events, when the gap after recovery is under 4 weeks
  - after the last event, when no undated goal wants a building block
  - for an off-season of keep goals
  - on request, through plan_block

BLOCK TYPES ARE WEEK PLANS, STORED AS DATA. A block type is a sequence of week kinds (BLOCK_WEEK_KINDS in m7-contract), each with its WeekTargets. m7-contract adds only optional keys (mainLifts, setsPerGroup {min, max, step}, running, combat and maintenance), stored in jsonb. So there is no migration, and old weeks read unchanged.
- Strength: accumulation, intensification and realization (peak weeks), and a meet sequence.
- Hypertrophy (accumulation weeks): setsPerGroup applies to M3's MAJOR_GROUPS, which M6 judges. Each week's range starts at the low end of M6's hardSetBand (M3's [10, 20]) and adds up to 2 sets a week (never more than 20 %), then a deload at 0.6.
- Marathon (marathon_* phases) and half (half_* phases):
  - base, build and peak weeks, then taper
  - at most +10 % a week, or up to +20 % when regaining a level held in the last 8 weeks
  - a cutback every 4th week, at 80 %
  - the long run grows 1.5 km a week, to 30 % of the week (35 % in peak), capped at 32 km or 3 h
  - race-specific work by phase. Marathon-pace segments use the steady kind at M pace, labelled 'at marathon pace'.
  - quality counts come from hooksFor(phase): M3's MARATHON_HOOKS for marathon phases, and HALF_HOOKS for half phases
- Fight camp (fight_camp):
  - 6–8 weeks, at most 2 hard sparring sessions a week, the last at least 7 days out
  - conditioning rounds, strength at maintenance, and a technical fight week
- Maintenance: every goal at its dose.
- Recovery: 1 week after a fight, 2 after a marathon.
- Deloads follow an experience cadence (new 5, novice and intermediate 4, advanced 3 loading weeks), or are reactive.
- Tapers:

  - a secondary event: a 3-day mini-taper; a low-priority event is trained through

- PLAN_BUDGET (rules/road.ts): at most 10 blocks, counting the past blocks a version keeps (programPlanSchema allows 12), and 300 decisions (of 500).

THE GENERATOR, AND WHAT M6 INHERITS: one serial chain, which starts after all of M6.
1. m7-stage-list (byte-identical): it moves the inline demand and blocks stages to their own files, and adds a prepare hook, a phasing stub (before volume), a schedule stub (last) and Draft.periodisation. It changes M6's next-block id to `next-block/1+${GENERATOR_ID}`.
2. generator-season: priorities, doses and season blocks, with one hunk each in M3's demand.ts, splits.ts and input.ts (modes). M3's superseded rules are marked; M3's maintenance rules stay active, because the doses read them.
3. generator-schedule: it repairs the hardest building week at real demands and applies the same moves to every building week, so a session keeps its day all block (M3's rule). An eased session's loads are recomputed at its new RPE.
4. generator-phasing: strength reps and RPE, hypertrophy sets and dose bands, through doseBand.
5. generator-running: VDOT paces, the long run, race-specific work, half hooks and cutbacks.
6. generator-combat: the fight camp.
7. next-cycle-periodised: M6's directives.ts and next-shape.ts read the season. M6's own id part becomes next-block/2.
8. hr-zones: the heart-rate input and decision only.
Rules for every slice in the chain:
- It replaces only its own stage file, plus the named hunks in M3 or M6 files that the single-owner table lists.
- It bumps GENERATOR_ID only when the same input could give a different plan (slices 2 to 6). next-cycle-periodised bumps only M6's part. hr-zones bumps nothing: a profile without heart rate gets the same plan, and one with it has a different input.
- Its PR lists every changed expectation across the expected-change surfaces, and runs them all:
  - M3's scenarios.test.ts and programming integration test
  - the journeys that generate programs (M3's program-journey, M4's journey-strength and journey-run-muay-thai, M6's journey-weekly-review and journey-cycle-review)
  - M6's next-block, next-block-store, cycle-review-service, next-cycle-apply and next-cycle-ui suites
  - M5's coach-journeys scripts that create programs
- It asserts PLAN_BUDGET headroom on longSeason, and from generator-schedule on, journeyHybrid's pinned first week.
After a bump, M3's build refuses a stale preview with reason 'profile', and M6's decideNextCycle returns ConflictError reason 'profile' for a stale next_cycle fingerprint, after which the cycle review re-previews, each as designed. M6 inherits the new stages by name. Re-plans inherit everything through generateProgram and generateNextBlock.

RE-PLANS ARE VERSIONS (ADR proposed in replan-domain). There are four directives and three mechanisms. Each makes one new version, through M5's lifecycle.
- priorities (new effective priorities) and block (a chosen phase, maintenance included) regenerate. A block that conflicts with a primary event is refused.
  - from: the first Monday from M3's next Monday (today when it is Monday) with nothing logged or skipped from it, so the week in progress is never rewritten
  - a block running across from is cut: re-inserted with the same lineage, ending the Sunday before
  - a block starting on or after from is replaced, never cut to zero weeks
  - from equal to the program's start regenerates the whole program through generateProgram at the same start
  - otherwise M6's generateNextBlock fills the new block: no bridge, continuity from the current phase, every still-eligible exercise kept, none rotated, loads from the latest e1RM and running from actual mileage
- taper splices:
  - the event-aligned block is cut at the taper's first Monday, or replaced when it starts there
  - taperSessions transforms the current weeks into the taper: the same days and exercises, less volume, intensity kept, one short strength session at least 4 days out
  - every block after the event is kept as shared rows
- deload rewrites one week in place, like M6's next-week ops:
  - the target is M6's next week for a review, or this or next week for the owner or coach
  - deloadSessions transforms its still-ahead sessions (values only), and the week becomes kind deload with deload targets, through M3's reviseProgram
  - nothing else changes
  - a deload, taper, event or recovery week in the target week or the two after it keeps M6's path instead
- storeReplan:
  - it validates the whole version with programPlanSchema
  - version N and every logged workout stay exactly as they were
  - it stores origin {'perfo-replan/1+' plus GENERATOR_ID, fingerprint, digest, input snapshot}
  - M6's reviewableBlock skips a block a re-plan cut short
- The weeks after a deload or taper keep their weekShapes digests, as tested.

PROPOSALS. There is one new M5 kind, replan. Its payload is {directive, from, baseVersionNumber, fingerprint, shapeDigest}, and the change is re-derived at accept.
- What the hashes cover:
  - fingerprint: today's profile input, the directive, the base version and from. It leaves out the actuals, so a logged set never invalidates it.
  - shapeDigest: phases, week kinds and dates, and the sessions' days, types and titles, but not loads.
- At accept:
  - a different fingerprint → superseded profile_changed
  - a different shape → plan_changed
  - a regenerate or splice whose from has passed or has something logged → start_passed
  - a deload with no still-ahead session left → M6's sessions_passed
  - a moved base → M5's program_changed
  - otherwise one new version, with loads refreshed and recorded; a repeated accept returns the stored result
  - for weekly_review provenance, the applier also writes M6's review_applied decision naming the review, so train-review-notice's weekChanges and the review link find it
  - every superseded state offers 'Propose again', and every refusal of 'Propose again' has a designed message
- Provenance: rules provenance gains the sources goal_priority and fatigue, reviews keep weekly_review, and the coach carries the thread.
- proposeReplan runs under the owner advisory lock, in the caller's executor. In a review's transaction it takes the lock again on the same session, which Postgres grants, and it never opens a second connection. Its context reads use the savepoint rule.
  - an open re-plan with the same directive kind and shape is returned
  - a different one is revised
  - an empty diff returns unchanged
- All M5 and M6 hot proposal modules change in one slice, replan-proposals, after M6's last editor (proposal-origin-label).

TRIGGERS.
- Goal changes: Profile's goal actions (save, reorder, status, delete) call replanForPriorities after their service commits. So does M5's acceptProposal, after commit, for an applied goal_update.
  - it compares effective priorities and event dates with the current block's snapshot; only a change runs a preview
  - it returns proposed, unchanged, deferred, no_program or failed in the action data
  - it never fails or delays the save
- Fatigue: when assessDeload triggers, the weekly review proposes a deload of M6's next week in place, instead of M6's −40 % ops. The snapshot stores boundary 'deload' with its reasons and no ops. It triggers on:
  - M6 fatigue 'high'
  - 'watch' plus a real e1RM decline on 2 or more main lifts, or an easy pace at least 3 % slower at the same RPE
  - a system overloaded on 5 of the last 7 days
- The weekly review handles a deload head like its own proposals:
  - decideNextWeek takes a replan head straight to acceptProposal or rejectProposal
  - refreshWeeklyReview re-runs assessDeload and proposeDeload for a deload review, and falls back to proposeNextWeek once a deload is no longer needed
  - getWeeklyReviewView's decisionState reads a replan head's status
  - the review's narration names the replan proposal and its decision state as data
- M6's path stays when a deload, taper, event or recovery week falls in the target week or the two after it, or when a deload ended within 14 days. M6's next-week rules also learn that recovery is light and a cutback is light for running.
- The cycle review uses next-cycle-periodised.
- The coach uses plan_block, schedule_deload and plan_taper, and proposes repairs to the owner's week through M5's propose_program_adjustment, passing the scheduler's ops.

COACH. Five tools join the programming group, in agent/tools/periodisation.ts. None of them drafts, because the engine builds the payload, so M5's 10 s tool deadline applies.

How the reads are bounded:
- On the pool (deps.db is the pool), they run in one short read-only transaction with SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '300ms'.
- Inside a caller's transaction (deps.db is a transaction), they run in a read-only savepoint with the same SET LOCAL. openQuestions: Event proximity: inside its lead window, an event goal leads ahead of a higher-ranked goal whose event is further away, and the plan explains it every time. The windows are fight 8 weeks, half 12, marathon 16, meet 10 and other race 6. Confirm these windows, or should your rank always win?

The coaching numbers are defaults, all listed in the rules reference:
- load model: the system shares, and the recovery half-lives (lower 2.5 days, upper 2, aerobic 1.5, combat 2, CNS 2)
- the acute:chronic ratio is the one Progress already shows (7- and 28-day averages), so it appears only after 28 days of training history; before that, only the half-lives judge fatigue
- overload at 1.5 × your own 28-day load
- evaluation costs: avoid 25 and prefer 8
- rank weights: 1, 0.6, 0.4, 0.25 and 0.15
Keep them?

Same-day order: when a day holds strength and a hard endurance or Muay Thai session, the higher-ranked goal's session goes first, at least 6 hours apart. M3 always put the run or the Muay Thai first. Confirm the 6 hours, and that strength goes first only when it ranks higher.

Re-plans for new priorities, a chosen block or a taper start on the next Monday with nothing logged from it, so the week in progress is never rewritten. Only a deload changes the week in progress, and only its sessions still ahead. Do you also want a 'from tomorrow' option for the others?
A re-plan for new priorities replaces the future weeks, including your own moves in them, and the proposal lists each one. Should your moves be carried over where they still fit instead?
Pausing or resuming a goal, changing an event date, and an accepted coach goal_update also propose a re-plan, not only a reorder. Is that right?

When the weekly review finds high fatigue or a real decline, it proposes a deload of the week after the reviewed one instead of M6's −40 % sets on the main lifts. The deload has lighter targets, no sparring and easy runs. If you review on Monday or later, only the sessions still ahead change. If a planned deload, taper, event or recovery week starts in that week or the two after it, M6's lighter adjustment is kept and the planned week does the rest. Confirm.

The weekly review now also judges its week and checks the moves it proposes with the new rules, on what you actually logged, so it may list a few more conflicts than before (for example hard sparring the day before heavy squats). Reviews stored earlier keep what they said. Is that right?
Deload cadence: a deload after every 5 loading weeks for a new lifter, 4 for novice and intermediate, and 3 for advanced, plus one at each block's end. Confirm.

Tapers:
- marathon: 3 weeks at 80/60/40 %
- half: 2 weeks at 70/50 %
- shorter races, meets and fights: 1 week; sparring stops at least 7 days before a fight
- a secondary event: a 3-day mini-taper
- a low-priority event: trained through, unless you ask the coach to taper it
Confirm.

Marathon defaults: at most +10 % a week, with one exception: regaining a level held in the last 8 weeks, at up to +20 %, always stated. A cutback every 4th week at 80 %, and a long run capped at 32 km or 3 hours. A half's build has 2 quality sessions a week. Confirm.

Marathon-pace work uses the existing 'Steady' segment type at your marathon pace, labelled 'at marathon pace', so workout logging and Progress need no new run type. Or do you want a separate 'Marathon pace' segment type everywhere?
Fight camp: 6–8 weeks, at most 2 hard sparring sessions a week, the last at least 7 days before the fight, and weight cutting out of scope. Confirm.

Maintenance doses reuse the program's existing maintenance style:
- strength and building muscle at maintenance: 1–2 'Keep' sessions, 2 sets an exercise, 4–10 hard sets per muscle group, with the main lifts' top set capped at RPE 8
- a secondary strength goal (one that does not lead but does not conflict with the leader) keeps its own split and style, at the lower half of its usual range: 8–11 sets for strength, 10–15 for building muscle
- running: 60–70 % of recent volume, with at most one quality session
- Muay Thai: technique and pads, with no sparring unless it is your class
In the four-goal example, build muscle is held at maintenance through fight camp and marathon build. Is that the trade-off you want?

Maintenance blocks hold every goal at its dose. They fill gaps of under 4 weeks between events, follow your last event when no goal wants a building block, make up an off-season of 'keep' goals, and are the whole plan when every goal is paused, as today. Should the season instead return to a building block for your top-ranked undated goal after the last event?

Heart rate: three optional fields in Profile → Running and in onboarding's running step (max, resting and threshold heart rate; one migration). Zones prefer threshold, then heart-rate reserve, then max. Or should zones come only from heart rate recorded in your runs?

Training paces move from Riegel to Daniels' VDOT, from your best race of the last 26 weeks (52 weeks at low confidence). A race with no date counts only when no dated race exists, and is treated as a rough guide. Confirm.
Train shows findings only for days still ahead, never for sessions already done, and shows no week summary on past weeks, outline weeks or bridge weeks. Is that right?
A block that a re-plan cuts short gets no cycle review of its own; the block that replaces it is reviewed at its end. Confirm.

A plan holds at most 10 blocks, counting past ones, so a year or more of re-plans can eventually ask you to start a new program from Today. Is that acceptable, or should old blocks be folded away instead?
Branches: the brief names feat/m7-advanced-coaching. This plan ships one PR per slice on m7/NN-* branches into main, as M3–M6 do. Confirm.
